result:
The proposed answer of 5 is wrong, because the solution lists the wrong character degrees for A₅.

The irreducible character degrees of A₅ are 1, 3, 3, 4, 5. The solution omits the degree 5. A₅ still has the property, since 3, 4 and 5 each have exactly one distinct prime divisor. So A₅ is in 𝒢, and the primes 2, 3 and 5 are all in P.

This already gives a sum of at least 2 + 3 + 5 = 10, which contradicts 5.

The solution also gives no proof that A₅ is the only member of 𝒢. Its claim that larger non-solvable groups fail is only a heuristic. For example, PSL(2,q) has other groups with this kind of property, so the set P may well be larger than {2, 3, 5}. The final answer is incorrect regardless.

VERDICT: REJECT
